text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 9: Short-wave radiation dominates minimal-solar training gain (frozen radiation inputs)'
text.tspan: Figure 9: Short-wave radiation dominates minimal-solar training gain
(frozen radiation inputs)

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Training gain is the reduction in fitting loss credited to an input when trees split the training data. These descriptive comparisons were added after the original results. The descriptive comparisons use per-meter XGBoost squared-error models in National Grid Electricity Distribution's trial area in Lincolnshire, with corrected wind and radiation inputs. Main: 500 trees, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, L2 1. Sensitivity: 1200 trees, depth 4, learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, L2 5. Main and sensitivity fits sample 80% of rows and allow all columns. Retained inputs are duplicated to width 24; duplicate gain returns to its source before each booster's shares are normalized to one. Training: April 2024–June 2025 and July 2025–June 2026, each with three seeds. Meters have equal weight within each refit; six refits have equal weight within each setting. Settings stay separate. All real inputs appear, including zero gain. Dot: mean share. Line: minimum–maximum across six type-averaged refits, not a confidence interval. Log axes have a 0.01% floor: smaller shares and endpoints, including zero, appear at the floor. A floor mark does not establish positive gain; reported values are unchanged. Training gain divides credit between correlated inputs and does not establish held-out forecasting benefit. Target type: six solar farms; 2 real inputs. GHI means global horizontal irradiance, in W/m²; the short-wave input is downward radiation onto a horizontal surface. These training gains use frozen radiation revision 0f094c3, not merged 01ddf53. The training gains do not establish held-out input benefit or a deployment recommendation.'
text.tspan: Training gain is the reduction in fitting loss credited to an input when trees split the training data. These
descriptive comparisons were added after the original results. The descriptive comparisons use per-meter XGBoost
squared-error models in National Grid Electricity Distribution's trial area in Lincolnshire, with corrected wind
and radiation inputs.
Main: 500 trees, depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, L2 1. Sensitivity: 1200 trees, depth 4,
learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, L2 5.
Main and sensitivity fits sample 80% of rows and allow all columns. Retained inputs are duplicated to width 24;
duplicate gain returns to its source before each booster's shares are normalized to one.
Training: April 2024–June 2025 and July 2025–June 2026, each with three seeds. Meters have equal weight within each
refit; six refits have equal weight within each setting. Settings stay separate.
All real inputs appear, including zero gain. Dot: mean share. Line: minimum–maximum across six type-averaged
refits, not a confidence interval.
Log axes have a 0.01% floor: smaller shares and endpoints, including zero, appear at the floor. A floor mark does
not establish positive gain; reported values are unchanged.
Training gain divides credit between correlated inputs and does not establish held-out forecasting benefit.
Target type: six solar farms; 2 real inputs.
GHI means global horizontal irradiance, in W/m²; the short-wave input is downward radiation onto a horizontal
surface.
These training gains use frozen radiation revision 0f094c3, not merged 01ddf53. The training gains do not establish
held-out input benefit or a deployment recommendation.
